correctness.rationale: Cubic DIMs are exactly independent-white/1-regular-black colourings; both linear vertex equations are necessary and sufficient. Summation forces 5|n. The matrix determinant equals Phi_5(z)R(z), where R is irreducible modulo 2 and cannot be one of the degree-four cyclotomics; hence every cyclic solution has period five. The outer word has exactly two nonadjacent zeros, giving five rotations, and the associated inner word satisfies the inner equations. Three executed standalone checkers corroborate independently: direct edge exact cover n=7..50, independent cyclic binary-word enumeration n=7..32, and integer-polynomial/length-five exhaustive checks. All claims are for n>=7, with no extrapolation from the finite tests.

originality.rationale: The closest family-specific source, Mahmoodi et al. (2024) Observation 7, constructs DIMs on GP(n,2) for 5|n, not an exact GP(n,3) census. General 2008 and 2014 work treats regular graph bounds and complexity, without an identified exact all-n third-step classification in the material examined. Targeted published-finding corpus queries and relevant earlier mathematical results revealed no covering equivalence, parameter shift, or stronger theorem. Uniform graph relabelling from the GP(n,2) claim is precluded at n=10 by bipartiteness of GP(10,3) and an odd inner cycle in GP(10,2). Unindexed literature and uninspected older full texts remain residual risks.

value.rationale: A natural exact-edge-covering invariant is completely classified for an infinite family of cubic generalized Petersen graphs. The step-three classification supplies a sharp arithmetic existence cutoff, the full labelled solution count, and unique cyclic pattern types. The spectral five-period rigidity is a substantive structural explanation rather than a new notation for 3n/5 cardinality. Known step-two existence does not determine this distinct family.
value.risk: Family-specific result only; no claim of a uniform all-step generalized Petersen theorem or broader algorithmic complexity improvement.
